name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 25 points after redistricting
Haynes has raised over $420,000 with $200,000 in outside support, versus minimal Republican fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 96 percent
model.rationale: The post-redistricting fundamentals point decisively Democratic, and the money gap is lopsided: Haynes has raised roughly 24 times what Jackson has, with outside spending on his side. Markets also price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at a Safe D margin near 26 points.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending for Jackson could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open Dallas-area seat after redistricting drew it as a strongly Democratic district, with a partisan lean of about 25 points. Frederick Haynes III, the Democratic nominee, has raised over $420,000 and holds nearly $120,000 on hand, supplemented by about $200,000 in outside support. Republican Everett Jackson has raised under $18,000 with barely $1,000 remaining.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 96 percent. With the district's fundamentals and the fundraising gap both pointing the same direction, this seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the winning margin rather than the outcome.
